summary: USFS cabin on Tom Dick Mountain, Mount Hood NF, Clackamas County OR; built 1933, removed or destroyed 1949. No source describes remains; mountain is a public hike.

facts.design: Cabin built by the USFS in 1933, not a tower (register); firelookout.com titles it a Fire Lookout Cabin
facts.status_note: Removed in 1949 per the register and the Oregon Lookouts page; destroyed in 1949 per firelookout.com
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mount Hood National Forest

access.note: The hike to the top starts at the Highway 26 Mirror Lake trailhead near Government Camp; the guide describes it as one of the most popular hikes in the forest. No source describes the cabin site itself.

visit.trail_note: Trail starts at the Highway 26 Mirror Lake trailhead, passes Mirror Lake and climbs steeply over rocky terrain in the last third of a mile before the summit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Oregon Lookouts say removed in 1949 and firelookout.com says destroyed in 1949. Same year; the method of ending differs. Both are reported and the story does not pick one.
The register uses Tom Dick Mountain; Wikipedia says the official name is Tom Dick and Harry Mountain after a 1969 decision, and that the older name was used in the past.

notes_for_editor: Brief kind 'ground' fits: this is a cabin, not a tower. Fate: register and Oregon Lookouts say removed 1949; firelookout.com says destroyed 1949. Name: the register's 'Tom Dick Mountain' is the older name of Tom Dick and Harry Mountain. Elevation: register 5,066 ft vs Wikipedia's highest peak 5,070 ft, not the same measurement. No source describes remains at the cabin site; a pile of rocks at the ridge top is described by a hiking guide without any link to the cabin. Access is public for the mountain (hiking trail) but no source addresses the cabin site specifically. Staffing not documented. The register's panorama photo is credited to the National Archives Pacific Northwest Region; no image URL was captured, so none recorded. Wikipedia cites an NGS datasheet named 'Tom Dick Lookout House' for the mountain's coordinates; it was not read, so it is not used.
